summary: EASD 2026 in Milan (Sep 28 to Oct 2) and EADV in Vienna produced a lot of named-drug GLP-1 news. These topics are not in our previous snapshots and look most promising: (1) Regeneron's COURAGE trial. Adding trevogrumab to semaglutide cut lean-mass loss by about half (-6.6% vs -3.4% at 26 weeks), and the paper is in press at The Lancet. It fits our muscle pillar and almost no creators have covered it yet. (2) Lilly's indirect comparison of tirzepatide (Zepbound) vs semaglutide 7.2 mg (Wegovy HD). People already search 'Wegovy HD vs Zepbound', so this is a headline decoder. (3) Novo's claims-data study of semaglutide 2 mg vs switching to tirzepatide: 6% lower MACE. Also a headline decoder: it's observational and funded by Novo. (4) Survodutide's first phase 3 paper in NEJM (SYNCHRONIZE-2: up to 13.1% vs 3.1% at 76 weeks). (5) Novo's '9 out of 10' liver-fat claim from STEP UP, which comes from a subgroup of only 26 people. (6) A JAMA study showing a 24-fold rise in GLP-1 prescriptions after childbirth. This one needs careful safety framing. (7) A Connecticut AG settlement that stops a platform selling 'research-grade' GLP-1s. This is an attributed-correction angle: we never name or link any source of the drug. We've already published on several fresh EASD items (nail detachment 39% vs 9%, ACHIEVE-4 mortality, EloraTZP, petrelintide), so I ranked those as follow-ups with new angles. Following the playbook, every candidate names a specific drug and a specific comparator. Competition checks are rough. Web results show news and pharma coverage, plus some telehealth blogs on Wegovy HD vs Zepbound. I couldn't count YouTube or TikTok videos directly, so the competition ratings are estimates from those results.

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: anti-myostatin antibody roughly halved lean-mass loss (COURAGE phase 2, EASD 2026, in press at The Lancet)
candidates.angle: 'Can a second drug stop semaglutide (Wegovy) taking your muscle?' At 26 weeks lean mass fell 6.6% on semaglutide + placebo vs about 3.4% (200 mg) and 3.9% (400 mg) with trevogrumab. The MRI substudy reported about 70% less muscle loss. Experimental only as of Oct 2026. Pivot to what works today: protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD Sep 30 and picked up by Reuters, Medical Xpress, News-Medical and Endpoints Oct 1. Muscle loss is one of the most-searched GLP-1 worries. Creator coverage is still thin, and a Men's Journal piece on Wegovy and muscle shows the consumer press is starting to pick it up.

evidence.signal: Phase 2 COURAGE: lean-mass loss reduced ~50%; MRI substudy ~70% less muscle loss; in press at The Lancet
-6.6% lean mass on sema+placebo vs -3.4%/-3.9% with trevogrumab at week 26, BMI ≥30
Data also on regaining muscle after stopping GLP-1 therapy

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) 15 mg vs semaglutide 7.2 mg (Wegovy HD): 4.5% more weight loss at 72 weeks in Lilly's indirect comparison (EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Is Zepbound really better than Wegovy HD?' The two trials alone show about 20.9% (SURMOUNT-1) vs about 20.7% (STEP UP). The 4.5-point gap comes from Lilly's own indirect, treatment-regimen analysis, and no head-to-head trial exists yet. Explain how one result can show both.
keywords: which weight loss shot works best
candidates.why_now: Lilly's release on Sep 29 was covered by Pharmacy Times on Oct 1. Wegovy HD is a new dose, and people actively search 'Wegovy HD vs Zepbound'. The confusing numbers (20.7 vs 20.9 against '4.5% more') make a clear decoder valuable.

evidence.signal: Zepbound 15 mg ~4.5% and 10 mg ~3.2% greater weight loss than Wegovy HD at 72 weeks (indirect, treatment-regimen)
'Tirzepatide Linked to More Weight Loss Than Semaglutide 7.2 mg', Oct 1
Independent indirect comparison of tirzepatide vs semaglutide in obesity without T2D, Sep 28

candidates.topic: Semaglutide 2 mg (Ozempic) escalation linked to 6% lower MACE vs switching to tirzepatide (Mounjaro) in type 2 diabetes: Novo real-world claims study (COMPETE SWITCH CV)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Is Ozempic safer for your heart than switching to Mounjaro?' The study covered 185,705 adults who moved up to semaglutide 2 mg and 23,104 who switched to tirzepatide. It was a retrospective, Novo-sponsored insurance-claims analysis, so it shows a link, not cause. The same congress also had real-world data favouring tirzepatide. Explain why company-funded real-world studies can disagree, and why switching is a decision for you and your prescriber.
keywords: semaglutide vs tirzepatide heart attack stroke
candidates.why_now: Novo's PR on Sep 29 was covered by HCPLive, Pharmacy Times (Oct 1) and Cardiovascular Business. Fierce Pharma framed EASD as Novo and Lilly 'pitting GLP-1s against one another'. The rivalry headlines are spreading to consumers.

evidence.signal: Ozempic 2 mg associated with lower MACE vs switching to Mounjaro, real-world EASD analysis
6% lower MACE; 185,705 vs 23,104; intention-to-treat claims data
Counterpoint: tirzepatide outperforms semaglutide in another real-world T2D analysis at EASD

candidates.topic: Survodutide (glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist): up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo weight loss at 76 weeks in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-2, NEJM)
candidates.angle: 'What is survodutide, and how does it compare with tirzepatide (Mounjaro)?' It's the first phase 3 paper for Boehringer's dual agonist. Explain the glucagon 'second engine' and its liver-fat angle. Make clear the trial compared it with placebo, not tirzepatide (mean 8.2%/9.8% by treatment-regimen vs up to 13.1%). Not approved as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Published in NEJM on Oct 1 at the same time as the EASD presentation, with Healio and AJMC coverage. Consumer coverage is minimal so far. Time and Patient Care 'next generation' roundups will drive searches for the name.

evidence.signal: 'Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes', Oct 1 2026
752 adults, T2D, BMI ≥27, 76 weeks; 'impressive' weight loss
8.2% (3.6 mg) and 9.8% (6 mg) mean loss; up to 79.3% reached ≥5% vs 32.7% placebo

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 now peer-reviewed in The Lancet: what the full paper adds (dose-by-dose results, side effects, dropouts) in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: 'Retatrutide's full paper is out: the numbers headlines skipped.' Name the actual figure each headline used (20.8% vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks, 18.8% by another estimand, '60 pounds'). Cover side-effect and stopping rates by arm. Add an attributed date hedge: not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026, and anything sold online isn't Lilly's trial drug.
candidates.why_now: Lancet publication on Sep 29, plus wide mainstream coverage (NBC, USA Today, Guardian 'Godzilla', Scientific American, CBS 'not yet FDA approved'). Searches about approval status keep growing. Our retatrutide Short is one of the top 4.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 RCT published Sep 29 2026
Substantial weight loss and A1C reduction in obesity + T2D
'Experimental weight loss drug yields big results, but not yet FDA approved'

candidates.topic: Semaglutide (Wegovy) and liver fat: Novo's '9 out of 10 reached normal' comes from 23 of 26 people in a STEP UP subgroup (post hoc, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did Wegovy really fix fatty liver in 9 out of 10 people?' Mean liver fat fell from 8.8% to 3.1% at 72 weeks. The 88.5% is 23 of 26 participants who started above 5%, in a post hoc analysis. Contrast it with the stronger evidence: semaglutide's MASH approval based on ESSENCE.
candidates.why_now: Novo's release on Oct 1 was carried by Yahoo Finance, Benzinga and RTT. The headline is catchy, but the small subgroup is the story nobody is telling. Fatty liver is an evergreen search with a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Wegovy reduced liver fat to normal levels in 9 of 10 adults with obesity and excess liver fat
STEP UP subgroup: 23 of 26 (88.5%) reached <5%, mean 8.8% → 3.1%

candidates.topic: GLP-1 prescriptions after childbirth rose 24-fold (0.08% to 1.9%, 2018–2025) in privately insured US mothers (JAMA, Oct 1)
candidates.angle: 'Starting Ozempic or Zepbound after having a baby? What the research does and doesn't know.' Explain the 1 in 6 figure (it applies to mothers with type 2 diabetes) and the gestational diabetes context. Say clearly that there's limited evidence on breastfeeding, and add pregnancy-planning context from the French Diabetologia study. The message is to plan it with your clinician, never to self-start. No postpartum 'bounce-back' framing.
candidates.why_now: JAMA study published Oct 1, covered by Medical Xpress, MedPage Today, News-Medical and PhillyVoice. Breastfeeding questions are a common worry with very little good content. The Diabetologia pregnancy-safety study (Sep 29) adds evidence.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 prescriptions for new mothers increased sharply; JAMA, Oct 1 2026
News pickup of the postpartum GLP-1 rise
French nationwide study on GLP-1 RA safety in pregnancy with T2D

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill: heart safety vs insulin glargine in ACHIEVE-4 (Lancet) plus Lilly's 'predicted' risk-reduction claim
candidates.angle: 'Is the Foundayo pill safe for your heart?' This is the long-form follow-up to our Short. The trial randomised 2,749 adults with T2D, overweight or obesity, and heart or kidney disease. Primary MACE-4 was 4.2% vs 5.0% (HR 0.84, non-inferior, not superior). The all-cause death result is nominal. Lilly's Oct 1 'predicted long-term risk' release is modelled, not measured.
candidates.why_now: Lancet paper on Sep 30, Medscape/Healio coverage Oct 1. A second Lilly release on Oct 1 about 'predicted' risk reductions is creating headlines that need decoding. Foundayo's brand searches are rising since approval.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4 orforglipron vs insulin glargine CV safety trial
HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20), 4.2% vs 5.0% MACE at median 2 years; A1C −1.6% vs −1.0%
Cardiovascular safety in largest, longest T2D study

candidates.topic: Connecticut AG settlement: platform agrees to stop selling 'research-grade' GLP-1s to US customers, citing impurities and inconsistent doses
candidates.angle: Attributed correction: 'Connecticut's attorney general says online 'research-grade' Ozempic and Mounjaro copies aren't the real thing.' Cover what regulators found (impurities, possible contamination, wrong amounts) and why approved, prescribed medicine matters. Never name or show sellers, prices or how to buy. Close by pointing to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: ABC News/GMA reported it on Oct 1. NetChoice's op-ed on the FDA's GLP-1 crackdown is also circulating. It follows the format of our #4 Short ('Lilly says online retatrutide isn't its trial drug').

evidence.signal: Online platform agrees to stop selling GLP-1 drugs to US customers
Primary source: settlement over unlawful 'research grade' GLP-1 sales

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails' follow-up: nail detachment 39% vs 9% and hair loss in GLP-1 users (EADV 2026, cross-sectional, self-reported) and what may help
candidates.angle: Searchable side-effect explainer with the exact scope. The study compared 575 GLP-1 users with 1,329 controls (only the controls are described as having T2D and/or obesity). Results were self-reported and cross-sectional, so they show a link, not cause. Weight loss alone didn't explain it. Cover the nutrition basics (protein with the kidney caveat), when to see a dermatologist, and not stopping medicine without talking to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: US News, MedPage, HCPLive, Medical Economics and Dermatology Times all covered it Oct 1–2, and EADV runs through Oct 3. We already covered it on 10-01, so this is only worth a different angle: a 'what to do' carousel or long-form combining hair and nails.

evidence.signal: Nail detachment 4x more common with GLP-1 use, first controlled study
39% vs 9% nail detachment; 575 users vs 1,329 controls
Users report more nail detachment and hair loss than nonusers

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1 medicines linked to higher heart attack, stroke and death risk: up to 22% at 2 years off in 333,000 US veterans with type 2 diabetes (WashU)
candidates.angle: 'What happens to your heart if you stop Ozempic or Mounjaro?' Show what happened to the people who stopped (observational, veterans with T2D). Pair it with the UGA finding that higher costs mean lower adherence, and frame it as a reason to plan any change with your prescriber. Never as advice to stop or keep taking a medicine.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots with momentum still in the mid-70s. A new UGA study (Sep 30) linking higher GLP-1 costs to lower adherence keeps the 'stopping' story going.

evidence.signal: Higher GLP-1 costs lead to lower adherence, Sep 30
Appeared in 5 snapshots, momentum 84→74, stage rising

candidates.topic: Switching from injections to the oral semaglutide (Wegovy) pill: 4.1% further average weight loss at 3 months (OCTANE real-world data, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does switching from the Wegovy shot to the Wegovy pill work?' The data come from telehealth records, are real-world and non-randomised, and run only 3 months. They don't show the pill beats the injection. Cover what to ask your prescriber about a switch and the pill's daily routine of taking it on an empty stomach.
candidates.why_now: Reported by CNBC, Reuters and MedicalDaily (Oct 2). KMOV's 'GLP-1 pills vs injections' segment shows consumers are asking. Momentum is slipping from 84 to 76, so publish soon or skip.

evidence.signal: Switchers lost 4.1% body weight on average after 3 months, EASD2026
People switching to Wegovy pill kept losing weight in real-world study

candidates.topic: Amylin drugs explained: CagriSema, eloralintide (EloraTZP) and petrelintide (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol) and why they're paired with GLP-1s
candidates.angle: Evergreen explainer refreshed by this week's news: 'What is amylin, and why is every new weight-loss combo adding it?' Explain the mechanism (fullness hormone, gastric emptying). Add a scorecard of the latest numbers with each trial's population and comparator. The MarketWatch and TradingView reports of more side effects with EloraTZP give a balanced point. None of these is approved as of Oct 2026, and the CagriSema US decision is expected in Q4 2026.
candidates.why_now: The petrelintide phase 2 paper came out Sep 29, the EloraTZP data are everywhere (New Scientist 'astonishing', Reuters, STAT), and a Diabetes Therapy review on amylin agonists was published Sep 28. People see 'amylin' in headlines without knowing what it is.

evidence.signal: Petrelintide ZUPREME-1 phase 2 RCT
Review: new amylin-based agonists for obesity and T2D
EloraTZP greater weight loss and A1C vs tirzepatide 15 mg in obesity + T2D

candidates.topic: Safiglipron: another once-daily oral small-molecule GLP-1 pill, randomised placebo-controlled trial in early type 2 diabetes (Nature Medicine)
candidates.angle: 'Beyond Foundayo: the next GLP-1 pills in the pipeline.' Explain how small-molecule pills differ from oral semaglutide (no fasting routine needed for orforglipron-type pills). Give safiglipron's trial population and results exactly, labelled as early-stage.
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine on Sep 29 with almost no consumer coverage. 'GLP-1 pill' searches are high after the Foundayo and Wegovy pill launches. Low search volume for the name itself makes this a pipeline-roundup piece, not a standalone Short.

evidence.signal: Safiglipron RCT in early T2D, Sep 29 2026

candidates.topic: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss: new Clinical Nutrition commentary, plus real-world tirzepatide body-composition data
candidates.angle: 'Should you take creatine on Mounjaro or Wegovy?' Answer honestly: the commentary proposes it, and dedicated RCTs in GLP-1 users are still lacking. Protein (with the kidney caveat) and resistance training have the stronger evidence. Pair with trevogrumab as 'the drug fix vs the gym fix'. Supplements need a clinician check, especially with kidney disease.
candidates.why_now: Creatine is a hot fitness search, and the trevogrumab news put GLP-1 muscle loss back in the headlines. Two new real-world tirzepatide body-composition papers (J Diabetes Complications, Obes Pillars) add data.

evidence.signal: 'Creatine for glucagon-like peptide-1-associated muscle loss'
Real-world 6-month tirzepatide effects on weight and body composition
Fat and lean mass during incretin therapy with structured exercise and nutrition support
